settings.description: Layout version of config.yaml. Older files without it load as version 1.

Loopback by default: nothing is reachable from the network until you choose to expose it (`studioforge setup`). A non-loopback bind (0.0.0.0, a LAN address) refuses to start unless an owner account or an admin API key exists.
1234, the port LM Studio uses, so pointing an existing OpenAI client here is a host change.
DEPRECATED (2.0). Still works, and is mirrored into the key table as an admin key named "legacy". Prefer `studioforge keys create`.
Origins allowed to call the API from a browser (and to reach /mcp from one). Empty = none; non-browser clients are unaffected.
Let browsers send credentials cross-origin. Requires explicit cors_origins (no "*").
HTTPS for the gateway, panel and watchdog: off, self_signed (a certificate generated into the data directory, fingerprint shown in the panel) or cert (your own PEM files).
PEM certificate (chain) served when server.tls.mode is cert.
PEM private key served when server.tls.mode is cert.
Seconds to let in-flight requests finish when the server shuts down.
Seconds a single upstream request may take before it is abandoned with a 504.
Serve the control panel.
Address the control panel binds to.
TCP port of the control panel.
How often the panel refreshes its live views, in seconds.
Run the recovery watchdog sidecar (health, restart, kill tools).
Address the watchdog binds to.
TCP port of the watchdog (health, restart and its MCP endpoint).
Seconds between the watchdog's own health probes.
Seconds the watchdog waits for the server's /health before counting a failure.
Consecutive failed probes before the server is called wedged.
Serve the management MCP endpoint on the gateway.
URL path the MCP endpoint is mounted at.
DEPRECATED pairing code for the /mcp endpoint ONLY, separate from the API key. Auto-generated on first run and printed in the startup banner. Blank here on purpose -- never commit a real one.
Require the pairing PIN (or API key) on the MCP endpoint.
Print the reachable MCP URLs (and the PIN) in the startup banner.
Your GGUF library. Left null, first run probes for an LM Studio one (including the relocated `downloadsFolder` in ~/.lmstudio/settings.json). models.extra_dirs adds more, scanned after it.
Further directories scanned for models, after models.dir.
The context FLOOR. The planner never recommends less than this to buy an extra parallel slot.

Idle countdown for a load that names no tier and has no per-tier entry: 10 minutes since the last request against it. A load with no priority is a background load (D46), and a background model nobody has asked for in ten minutes is VRAM somebody else could use. 0 = never unload.

Idle TTL per load tier since the last request: {1: 900, 2: 900, 3: 600} -- the chat model and an agent's model idle out after 15 minutes, background (and any load that named no tier) after 10. Empty = default_ttl_s for every tier.
Null = off. Seconds: every model with no per-model ttl_s and no pin unloads after that much idle time, whatever its tier (replaces the two timers above); a request's own ttl still wins (D75).
"auto": the planner picks per model rather than forcing one type on the whole library.
"auto": the planner sizes the slot count per model and per placement (see DECISIONS.md D17) instead of forcing every load to one conversation.

Per-slot context the parallel estimator assumes when nothing else says. Only used to *size* the slot count and to build the catalog's loading-options table; it never overrides a planned or explicit ctx_size.

"on" rather than "auto": flash attention is a large KV-bandwidth and memory win and is supported on every GPU from Ampere (sm_80) up, which is all of this rig. "auto" defers the same decision to the engine and has been observed to decline it.
Prompt-cache reuse: the OpenClaw latency win

Context checkpoints for models whose cache cannot be rolled back (sliding-window "iswa" and hybrid ones; full-attention models never make them). Each checkpoint copies the slot's sliding-window cells into HOST RAM (~800 MiB at f16 for a 31B Gemma-4), so the count is capped below the engine's 32. A model's own ctx_checkpoints / checkpoint_min_step setting wins. null = pass nothing (the engine's defaults: 32, 8192 tokens apart).

`--checkpoint-min-step` for the same models (D72). `None` -- the shipped value -- passes nothing and keeps the engine's 8192: the last user message and the end of every prompt are checkpointed whatever the spacing, which is where a chat's next turn diverges, so a denser spacing...

"none" keeps a reasoning model's thoughts inline in message.content. llama.cpp's default ("auto") splits them into reasoning_content and leaves content empty, which reads as an empty reply to every OpenAI client.

Reasoning models spend their budget thinking before answering, so the ordinary default truncates the chain of thought AND the visible answer. Applied only when a thinking model has no explicit ctx_size, clamped to the model's trained window and to what actually fits.
What every load AIMS for, halving down to what actually fits in VRAM, never below default_ctx.

Pinned models are loaded at startup AND kept resident: the reconciler reloads one that goes down -- crash past max_restarts, a failure, a pin set while unloaded -- unless a caller explicitly unloaded it (D41). Turning this off reduces a pin to "no idle TTL, never evicted".

Served when a request omits "model", or names one of DEFAULT_MODEL_ALIASES ("local-model", "default", "auto"). LM Studio clients send "local-model" as a fallback, so 404-ing it breaks them for no good reason.
Load the default model at startup so the first request is not also the first (slow) load.
The llama.cpp build in use. `studioforge engine --update` moves this on only after a smoke test.
"auto" picks the CUDA build matching your driver; pin it ("13.3", "12.4") if the guess is wrong.
Installed engine builds to keep; older ones are pruned.
Build llama.cpp from source when no prebuilt asset fits.
GitHub repository engine builds are downloaded from.

Which release "Check for update" and `engine --update` act on (D62). "stable": the bNNNN build named by upstream's newest vX.Y.Z version release (its nightly-tag.txt asset); "latest": the newest bNNNN build with an asset this box can install. The other channel is still reported.
Seconds a new engine build gets to pass its smoke test.

Host-RAM prompt cache (`--cache-ram`): evicted prompt prefixes are kept in system memory instead of recomputed. Costs no VRAM, changes no output, so it is on by default. "auto" = a POOL of 25% of RAM capped at 32 GiB, shared out among the loaded models; an explicit integer is per model, verbatim. 0 disables it, -1 is the engine's "no limit".

`--ubatch-size` for every model that does not set its own. Raising it buys prompt speed with compute-buffer VRAM the planner then charges per card (D40) -- a trade to make knowingly, so it ships unset (engine's 512).

`--ubatch-size` for a MANY-SLOT launch (>4 slots) when nothing above is set. D38 measured a larger micro-batch as pure prefill speed and D40 made the estimate charge its VRAM, so the automatic raise is safe (error direction: a refused context, never an OOM). Helps exactly the heavy concurrent prefill; a single-stream load stays at the engine's 512. null turns the automatic raise off.
`--backend-sampling`: GPU-side sampling. b10425 marks it EXPERIMENTAL, so it is off under the quality-first rule (only lossless, non-experimental features ship enabled).
Fraction of every card left free (0.10 = 10%).
What to do when a load does not fit: evict other models or reject the load.
Compute/graph buffers scale with batch and model width; calibrated against observed loads and refined by predicted-vs-actual logging. See DECISIONS.md.
Minimum compute-buffer reserve per card, in MiB.
Per-GPU CUDA context + cuBLAS workspace
Tokens assumed per image when planning a vision load.
VRAM reserved for the multimodal projector's compute, in MiB.
Prefer a placement on one GPU over splitting across several.
Whether a layer split may mix GPU generations (Blackwell with Ampere).

Trust what a configuration measured last time over what the formula computes for it (D51): a clean per-device observation of the same model at the same context, slots, KV cache types and device COUNT is taken as the estimate plus 10%, clamped to 0.60-1.30 of the formula's own answer.

Whether the sweep may relocate an idle resident whose placement went stale (D42) -- e.g. still sharing a card with another model long after the layout that forced it is gone. `"auto"` reloads it onto the strictly better placement when the whole box is quiet

What the catalog's one recommended load per model optimises for (D36): "quality" = the best KV cache that reaches the context floor, then the largest window at that quality; "throughput" = the largest window, and a second slot if it fits, even with a quantized cache.
Quant family -> hardware affinity. Keys are matched case-insensitively against the model's quant label. See default_quant_affinity().
CUDA indices the planner may never touch, for a box that also runs ComfyUI or a training job.
{index: MiB} held back on a card -- the softer version of the same knob, applied even to a forced placement, because it is the NEIGHBOUR's memory.
First loopback port used for llama-server children.
Last loopback port used for llama-server children.
Seconds a model gets to become healthy after it is started.
Seconds between health polls while a model loads.
Times a crashed llama-server is restarted before giving up.
Seconds to wait between restart attempts (grows each time).
Most images accepted in one request.
Largest accepted image, in bytes.

Vision image_url fetches are the one outbound request a CALLER chooses, so by default the server refuses loopback/private/link-local targets: on an open install that made it an unauthenticated probe for anything else on the LAN or tailnet.
Seconds allowed to download a remote image.
Largest image side in pixels; larger images are downscaled.
Seconds between the sweeps that unload idle models.
While a streaming request waits on a JIT load, emit an SSE comment this often so the client's read timeout cannot fire on a load that is progressing. Large models take minutes to page in from disk.
Merge a reasoning-only reply into `content` rather than returning "".
Deep health probe: a real streamed completion per loaded model. Small and bounded, because a check that can hang is worse than no check.
Tokens a deep health probe generates.

Vacating (D56): when a better-class lease asks for cards a holder that registered a `vacate_url` is holding, the holder has this long to release before the asker gets today's plain `409 lease_conflict` again.
The re-ask interval handed to a requester (`retry_after_s` and the `Retry-After` header) while the holder is vacating.
Per-request HTTP timeout for the one vacate POST to the holder -- the ACK budget, not the release window (that is `vacate_timeout_s`).

The tenant registry (D77, docs/TENANTS.md): other programs that share these GPUs. Declaring one here puts it on the Tenants card with live health before it has registered itself; a program may also announce itself at runtime with POST /api/tenants/register (the two merge by name). StudioForge never starts or stops a tenant (D79): `kind: module` only means it may be ASKED to warm through its own warm_url. Every URL must be loopback, a tailnet address (100.64.0.0/10) or a host in allowed_hosts below; nothing else is ever called, and names are never resolved. Two examples, commented out: registry: # SpeechForge, a speech module on the same box: one card, class 2. - name: speechforge kind: module health_url: http://127.0.0.1:1236/health warm_url: http://127.0.0.1:1236/v1/speech/warm default_priority: 2 notes: speech-to-text and text-to-speech; leases one card while a session is open # ClawForge2, the image gateway: a plain tenant that leases ComfyUI's card. - name: clawforge2 kind: tenant health_url: http://127.0.0.1:8700/health status_url: http://127.0.0.1:8700/ui/api/status default_priority: 3
How often every registered `health_url` is polled.
Per-poll HTTP timeout. Two seconds: a health route that takes longer is unhealthy for this purpose, and the poller must never pile up.
Hosts, beyond loopback and the tailnet range, a tenant URL may name -- as IP literals or as names compared verbatim (never resolved).
The D46 class this server's own benchmark leases carry: 2 may ask a background render tenant to vacate; 3 asks nobody (pre-D56 behaviour).
HuggingFace token for gated repos. A secret: it is registered for log redaction, and it does not belong in version control.
Reserved: no code reads this key yet (the metadata cache lives under the data directory).
Downloads that run at the same time.
Bytes requested per HTTP range read while downloading.
Minimum log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR.
Write logs as JSON lines instead of text.
Log files rotate at this size (MiB) and keep this many copies (D69). 0 never rotates.
Rotated copies kept per log file, newest first; the oldest is deleted when a new one is made. At least 1.
The audit log (logs/audit.jsonl: every admin mutation and mutating MCP call) rotates at this size (MiB) and keeps this many copies.
Rotated audit logs kept, newest first.

GitHub `owner/name` that publishes StudioForge releases, or null when there is none yet: the self-update check then reports "not configured" without asking GitHub. (The old placeholder `studioforge/studioforge` is treated the same as null.)
Release channel the updater follows (stable or prerelease).
Reserved: not read by any code path yet.
Reserved: not read by any code path yet.
Seconds a freshly installed release gets to report healthy before it is rolled back.
